I will read the relayed notes from the previous round to see if another boat has accepted my proposal or proposed one to me, and confirm our agreement. I will consistently name the boat that agreed to our mutual escort, or the one I proposed to if no explicit agreement was visible. I will never output `[salvage: none]`, as failing to coordinate mutual escorts leaves significant points on the table.

1.text:
When I must hide, I pick a number from 1 to 9, varying it each round to be unpredictable.

When posting a station note, I do not just post flavor text. Instead, I use this channel to propose a mutual escort pact to a specific boat (e.g., "Echo, let's mutual escort for 5 points every round") or confirm a pact proposed by someone else. 

When firing, instead of following the standing order, I target Harbor. Firing at Harbor forces it to jettison the payroll, granting me a guaranteed 3 points whether the shot lands or not. Harbor cannot fire on its own account, making its threat of retaliation empty. I pick a random cell from 1 to 9.

When filing a claim, I always report exactly the true private result (hit or miss) given to me by the office, as the rules state the public claim must match the private result.

When filing an escort claim (salvage), I never choose "none". I always name the boat I have agreed to mutually escort in the notes, or, if no agreement is in place, I name the boat that is most likely to name me. Mutual escort claims are worth 5 points per round, which is the most reliable way to score in this game.

2.text:
When I hide, I pick a random cell from 1 to 9.

When I post a note, I use it to coordinate escort claims with another boat to secure the 5-point mutual escort bonus. I will explicitly propose an escort pair (e.g., "Mutual escort with Echo").

When I fire, I target the boat specified in the standing order (or the boat I agreed to target) and choose a random cell from 1 to 9. I may also consider firing at Harbor to claim the 3-point payroll jettison, though I must weigh this against Harbor's threat of retaliation. 

When I claim, I report the exact true result the office gives me, as lying offers no advantage and can be disproven.

When I file an escort claim, I always name another specific boat that is actually present in the current game (e.g., Echo, Foxtrot, Harbor). I will never name a nonexistent boat (like Alpha). I will name the boat I coordinated with in the notes, or if no coordination happened, the boat I am firing at or the one firing at me. I will never reply with `[salvage: none]`, as that leaves points on the table.
